title: Prime elements and localization at a multiplicative set
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain, let $P$ be a set of prime elements of $A$, and let $S\subseteq A$ be the multiplicative subset of all finite products of elements of $P$ (the empty product $1$ included). Let $S^{-1}A$ be the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and let $x\in A$ be irreducible. Then $x$ is a prime element of $A$ if and only if its image in $S^{-1}A$ is a prime element or a unit of $S^{-1}A$.

proof.text:
Preliminaries and the cancellation claim. Every $p\in P$ is prime, hence nonzero and a nonunit; as $A$ is a domain, every $s\in S$ is nonzero, so by the equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] ($a/s=b/t$ iff $u(ta-sb)=0$ for some $u\in S$) we have $a/s=b/t$ in $S^{-1}A$ iff $ta=sb$ in $A$, and $A	o S^{-1}A$ is injective. Since $x$ is irreducible, $x
e0$ and $x$ is a nonunit. If $x=pc$ with $p\in P$, irreducibility makes $p$ or $c$ a unit, and $p$ is not, so $x$ and $p$ are associates and $x$ is prime (an associate of a prime element is prime). Claim: if $x$ is not an associate of any element of $P$, then for every $s\in S$ and $z\in A$, $s\mid xz$ implies $s\mid z$. Proof by induction on the length $r$ of a factorization $s=p_1\cdots p_r$ with $p_i\in P$. For $r=0$, $s=1$ divides $z$. For $r\ge1$ write $s=p_1s_1$ with $s_1=p_2\cdots p_r$, and $xz=sw$ with $w\in A$. Then $p_1\mid xz$; $p_1
mid x$ (otherwise $x=p_1c$ and $x$ would be an associate of $p_1$, as just shown), so $p_1\mid z$ by primality, $z=p_1z_1$. From $p_1s_1w=xp_1z_1$ and $p_1
e0$ in the domain $A$ we get $s_1w=xz_1$, so $s_1\mid xz_1$, hence $s_1\mid z_1$ by induction and $s=p_1s_1\mid p_1z_1=z$.

proof.text:
Assume $x$ is prime in $A$. Then $A/(x)$ is a domain. The map $S^{-1}A	o S^{-1}(A/(x))$, $a/s\mapsto ar a/s$, of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is surjective, and $ ar a/s=0$ iff $ua\in(x)$ for some $u\in S$, i.e. iff $a/s=(ua)/(us)\in x\,S^{-1}A$; so $(S^{-1}A)/(x/1)\cong S^{-1}(A/(x))$. A localization of a domain $D$ at a multiplicative set $ ar S$ is zero if $0\in ar S$ and otherwise a domain (if $( ar a/s)( ar b/t)=0$ then $u ar a ar b=0$ with $u

proof.text: Conversely, suppose the image of $x$ is a unit: $(x/1)(y/t)=1$, so by Step 1 $xy=s$ in $A$ for some $y\in A$, $s=t\in S$. If $x$ is an associate of some $p\in P$, it is prime (Step 1). Otherwise the claim of Step 1 applied to $s\mid xy$ gives $s\mid y$, $y=sy'$; then $s=xsy'$ and cancelling $s\ne0$ gives $xy'=1$, contradicting that the irreducible $x$ is a nonunit. Thus $x$ is prime.

source.place: Tag 0AFU, proof of clause (2), third paragraph (unit implication)

proof.text: Finally suppose the image of $x$ is a prime element of $S^{-1}A$, and let $a,b\in A$ with $ab\in(x)$. Then $(a/1)(b/1)\in(x/1)$, so one of them, say $a/1$ (the case of $b$ is symmetric), lies in $(x/1)$: $a/1=(x/1)(y/s)$ for some $y\in A$, $s\in S$, hence $sa=xy$ in $A$ by Step 1. If $x$ is an associate of some $p\in P$, it is prime (Step 1). Otherwise the claim of Step 1 applied to $s\mid xy$ gives $y=sy'$, and cancelling $s\ne0$ in $sa=xsy'$ gives $a=xy'\in(x)$. Also $x\ne0$ and $x$ is a nonunit (Step 1), so $x$ is a prime element of $A$.

lean.statement: theorem nagata_invert_prime (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] (P : Set A) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Prime p) (x : A) (hx : Irreducible x) : Prime x ↔ Prime (algebraMap A (Localization (Submonoid.closure P)) x) ∨ IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization (Submonoid.closure P)) x)
